skill.name: readability
skill.description: Analyze text readability with Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, and other metrics. Returns objective scores with interpretation and recommendations.
skill.summary: Measure readability scores and get clear recommendations for improving English prose.
skill.author: humanizerai

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by readability terminology and a Markdown code fence. The skill is a documentation-only prompt for calculating readability metrics and does not contain executable commands, network access, or prompt injection text.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 40 starts a Markdown fenced example for the output format, not Ruby or shell execution. No executable command or user-controlled command path appears in the skill.
Line 23 documents the Flesch-Kincaid readability formula and uses 'US grade level' as an education metric. It does not request system information or environment reconnaissance.
Line 47 is an output table placeholder for a Flesch-Kincaid grade score. It is readability reporting text, not system reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Readers leave when text is too complex or unclear. This skill scores readability and recommends clearer wording for the right audience.
actual_capabilities: Calculates Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch-Kincaid grade estimates.
Calculates Gunning Fog and SMOG index estimates.
Reports word count, sentence count, and average sentence length.
Estimates complex word percentage and passive voice sentences.
Identifies likely audience level from readability scores.
Suggests specific edits for shorter, clearer prose.
limitations: Syllable counts and passive voice checks are heuristic estimates.
It does not verify factual accuracy, tone, or legal compliance.
It needs pasted text and does not fetch external documents.
It works best for English prose.

use_cases.title: Prepare Public Articles
use_cases.description: Check whether a draft article fits the reading level of a broad public audience.

use_cases.title: Improve Help Documentation
use_cases.description: Find long sentences and complex words before publishing product support content.

use_cases.title: Review Product Copy
use_cases.description: Measure onboarding text and prioritize edits that reduce reading effort.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Readability
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this text for readability. Give scores, audience level, and three simple fixes: [paste text].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a quick first pass on a draft.

prompt_templates.title: Improve A Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this draft for a general audience. Highlight difficult sentences, complex words, and clear rewrite priorities: [paste text].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you need actionable editing guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Versions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these two versions for readability. Explain which is easier to read and why: [paste version A and version B].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when choosing between alternate drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Audit For A Target Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this text for readers at an eighth grade level. Report scores, risks, and the most important edits: [paste text].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when readability must match a defined audience.

output_examples.input: A customer support article with long sentences and technical terms.
output_examples.output: The report shows a high grade level, long average sentence length, and several complex words. It recommends shorter sentences and simpler terms.

output_examples.input: Two versions of onboarding text for a mobile app.
output_examples.output: The comparison identifies the easier version, explains score differences, and lists edits that improve clarity without changing meaning.

output_examples.input: A policy notice intended for a general audience.
output_examples.output: The analysis estimates audience level, flags dense wording, and suggests plain language changes for clearer public communication.

best_practices: Provide the complete text and intended audience.
Ask for both scores and edit recommendations.
Review suggested changes for meaning before publishing.
anti_patterns: Using readability scores as the only quality measure.
Testing very short fragments and treating results as final.
Using the skill instead of expert legal or medical review.

faq.question: Does this skill rewrite my text?
faq.answer: It focuses on scoring and recommendations. You can ask for rewrite suggestions after the analysis.

faq.question: Which readability formulas does it use?
faq.answer: It covers Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade, Gunning Fog, and SMOG.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The user provides the text directly in the prompt.

faq.question: Can it analyze non-English text?
faq.answer: It works best for English. Formula results may be unreliable for other languages.

faq.question: Can it detect passive voice?
faq.answer: It can estimate passive voice sentences. The result should be reviewed by a human editor.

faq.question: Are the scores exact?
faq.answer: No. Scores depend on sentence splitting, syllable estimates, and text length.
